stem: Which of the following is true regarding 'head banging' as a rhythmic activity in children?

options.text: It typically begins at the end of the first year and stops before age $4$
It is significantly more common in females than in males
It is usually associated with abnormal daytime behavior or development
It rarely occurs in children who have previously shown body rocking

explanation: Head banging is a common rhythmic movement disorder of early childhood that most children outgrow by school age.
rationale: Consider the typical age range and developmental context for this behavior.

optionExplanations.A: Head banging is a common rhythmic movement disorder of early childhood that most children outgrow by school age.
optionExplanations.B: The source material notes that head banging is actually more common in males.
optionExplanations.C: Most children who exhibit head banging at bedtime show normal development and behavior during their waking hours.
optionExplanations.D: Head banging is often preceded by other rhythmic activities like body rocking.
